_comment: One file, the whole surface (ADR-019 D4) -- consumed as CSS custom
properties by apps/web/scripts/tokens-to-css.mjs. Android and iOS read
this same file when a shell exists to hold it.
The register question closed 2026-07-25 (Kihea, ADR-019's final
amendment) and ADVISORY-008 corrected the picker that re-asked it: the
reading state has one material, not two. `page.*` is the passage's own
ink-and-paper (ADR-019 Decision 1, untouched by any of this); `chrome.*
is the room the page floats in -- dark-first glass and metal, the
vision register (interface-inspiration/vision.md), scoped to what
ADVISORY-008 §1's floor and §3's material calls actually require for a
single reading screen. Values here are still provisional -- they are a
concrete embodiment for Kihea's eyes at item 7, not the M1.5 prototype
finding ADR-006 asks for -- and every one of them should move once
someone has looked at this on a real screen with real text, in both
themes, for more than a few minutes.
ADVISORY-008 §2, the architect's taste calls, handed down for this
circuit and not reopened here: ground is ink with a blue bias, not
near-black and not a reflex cream tint; the aura is what glass has to
refract or it is a grey box; the metal hairline is two backgrounds and
two clips, not a 1px border; one warm accent (brass) carries every
action, and the cool tone appears only inside edge-light gradients,
never as an accent.
T5 additions (DERIVATION-003), chrome-only -- none of these are read by
any reading-state component. `motion.durationChromeTransition` is a
new, distinct 420ms -- it is NOT durationSlow (460ms) or durationBeam
(900ms), both load-bearing inside the reading state (PassagePage.css,
GlossCard.css) and out of scope to rename. `motion.durationLoopIdle` is
C1's 1400ms loop period, the one candidate token that outlived the
breathing dot it was drawn for -- it drives the orb's idle morph and
the loader's rotation, never a one-shot transition. `easingSpringLoud`
is the second, louder spring for chrome bounce (icon-swap confirm, D5's
card); `easingSpring` stays reserved for the Switch knob alone, per the
design system's own readme and D4's verdict. `chrome.*.glassBg/
glassBorder/glassBlur/glassHighlight` and `chrome.*.shadowFloat` are the
orb and loader's floating-glass material (DERIVATION-003 C3). Two
candidate tokens are deliberately absent: `--dur-5` (640ms) and
`--press-scale-loud` (.93) -- DERIVATION-003 finds no surviving variant
adopts either.

font.serif: 'Source Serif 4 Variable', ui-serif, Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif

page._comment: The passage's own paper surface -- ADR-019 Decision 1: the register question and everything in `chrome` below stop at the text column. This is the same object in every mode; it never inverts, because a lit page held up in a dark room is the whole point of dark mode reading at night (superb-craft/reading-surface.md).

dark._comment: Not currently wired to any component -- the reading card always takes page.light, dark-first chrome around it. Kept for a future surface that sets the passage in a genuinely dark room rather than a lit one.

chrome._comment: The room the page floats in. Dark-first, blue-biased ink -- not near-black, not the cream tint superb-craft names as its own tell. `glowA`/`glowB` are the aura: two large, diffuse, low-opacity lights so the metal edge has something to refract. `glowB` and `metalEdge3` are the one place the cool tone is allowed to exist -- it never carries an action or a state. `metalEdge1/2/3` are the 135deg gradient stops for the two-background, two-clip hairline (design/metal.css); nothing here is a plain border. `accent` is brass, and it is the only colour any control, focus ring, or state uses.
